guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Adult Basic Life Support 2021
title: Collapse at a football tournament
setting: First aid cover at a football tournament. A player, 56M, collapsed on the pitch. Lying still, not moving, pale with a grey, bluish tinge to the lips.
verdictExplanation: Unresponsive and not breathing normally after a sudden collapse. This is cardiac arrest, the most time-critical emergency. Unequivocally sick: start CPR and use an AED immediately.

shared.airway: Can be opened, patient cannot maintain own airway

history.history: Collapsed suddenly while playing, no warning

followUp.question: What is your immediate action?

options.text: Start chest compressions, send for an AED and call 999
Place him in the recovery position and wait
Give two rescue breaths only and reassess in a minute
Sit him up and offer a sip of water

followUp.explanation: Unresponsive and not breathing normally means cardiac arrest. Begin chest compressions at once, get someone to fetch the AED and call 999. The recovery position is for unresponsive patients who ARE breathing normally.

levelExplanation.cfa: Push hard and fast in the centre of the chest (about 5-6 cm, 100-120/min) and apply the AED as soon as it arrives.
levelExplanation.er: Deliver high-quality CPR with minimal interruptions, attach the AED and manage the airway with your available adjuncts.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Early CPR and early defibrillation give the best chance of survival. Do not delay compressions.
